deep_research_gate_rule.rule: No new area gets a deep research bind unless failure to resolve it prevents us from explaining how the system works.

classification_scheme.COVERED: Structurally framed enough for book architecture; may still need later validation
classification_scheme.NEEDS_DEFINITION: Must be defined well enough to fit the system before the book skeleton is complete
classification_scheme.NEEDS_FIRST_PASS_STRUCTURE: Needs a light structural write-up; not a research campaign
classification_scheme.IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_LATER: Gap acknowledged; deferred past first complete skeleton

master_audit_areas.why_essential: The whole system has to fund itself without personal income/property taxes
Who creates credit, who gets it, and where interest flows determines local prosperity
Housing cost, land speculation, zoning, ownership, and property access shape nearly every household outcome
Work, healthcare, school, aging, rural access, and logistics depend on mobility
Water rights, watersheds, extraction, agriculture, industry, and long-term resilience
Broadband, public data, cybersecurity, digital identity, AI access, cloud infrastructure
Wages alone are insufficient; bargaining power, ownership, portability, scheduling, benefits matter
Pathway from worker → owner → local employer → local capital formation
Monopoly, consolidation, franchise extraction, private equity, and absentee ownership drain local wealth
Rules for where public and private capital goes and what returns stay local
Health, crop, property, disaster, liability, and business insurance can silently determine system viability
master_audit_areas.note: First-pass structure in book; deep bind only if unexplained system failure

master_audit_areas.why_essential: Incarceration, fines, re-entry, employment barriers, and community reintegration are economic architecture
Police, fire, EMS, disaster response, and emergency capacity are core public goods
Childcare is workforce infrastructure affecting labor participation, fertility, education, and household surplus
Retirement concepts exist; full care economy for older Arkansans does not
Economic participation requires mobility, employment, care, housing, and service accessibility
Arkansas must decide who it wants to retain, attract, educate, and integrate
master_audit_areas.note: HYP-132 framed; deepen inside structural locks where needed, not as a new research lane

master_audit_areas.why_essential: Public dollars can leak out or deliberately build Arkansas firms and supply chains
Cities/counties need a revenue model after property-tax dependence is reduced or eliminated
State/local/federal responsibilities, grants, preemption, and fiscal transfers must fit together
Distinguish money earned from Arkansans versus money imported into Arkansas
master_audit_areas.note: External Income / EICR architecture exists; COUNTABLE $0; refine inside LOCK-01

master_audit_areas.why_essential: External-income engines and community-identity assets
Information markets shape democracy, civic trust, rural access, and political power
Integrated AI/state systems require strong limits on surveillance and data abuse
Re-engineering government requires explicit constraints on government itself
Agencies, boards, authorities, performance rules, sunset reviews, and accountability need redesign
Economic reform fails if concentrated wealth can buy the rules back
GDP, tax revenue, jobs, and wages do not fully measure household prosperity or capital retention
master_audit_areas.note: Lock definitions inside household-economics OS layer; no new research lane

master_audit_areas.why_essential: Move from today’s system to the new one without breaking pensions, services, credit, or markets

operating_system_questions.title: Ownership
operating_system_questions.question: For every major asset class—land, energy, housing, infrastructure, IP, utilities, processing, healthcare, finance—who owns it, who controls it, who bears the risk, and who receives the surplus?

operating_system_questions.title: Capital formation
operating_system_questions.question: How does Arkansas turn current production into future productive assets—savings, investment, public capital, pension capital, local equity, credit, and reinvestment?
operating_system_questions.book_role: Centered in LOCK-02; appears across LOCK-01/04/06

operating_system_questions.title: Market design
operating_system_questions.question: What rules make markets produce broad prosperity instead of extraction—competition policy, public options, cooperatives, procurement, ownership incentives, anti-monopoly?

operating_system_questions.title: Household economics
operating_system_questions.question: Does an Arkansas household have enough income, assets, time, security, housing, healthcare, transportation, food, education, and retirement capacity to build a good life?
operating_system_questions.book_role: Ultimate unit of measurement; queued Household Prosperity Surplus panel remains future validation

operating_system_questions.title: Power
operating_system_questions.question: How does the system prevent economic concentration from reconcentrating political power?
operating_system_questions.book_role: May be one of the most important ideas in the project; centered in LOCK-09; constrains all other locks

ten_structural_locks.title: Transportation, water, digital, and core infrastructure

Transition architecture from the current system to the new one
